source.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
source.authors: Hunar Batra; Lachin Naghashyar; Ashkan Khakzar; P. Torr; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Constantin Venhoff; Ronald Clark

page_placements.theme: Correspondence of SAE features across models, finetunes, domains and pruning

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses feature correspondence and explicitly mentions splitting and merging, but does not test whether increasing SAE dictionary size produces splits.
record.gate_note: No comparison across SAE dictionary sizes or test of larger-versus-smaller dictionaries is reported. Appendix E.2 reports feature matching between same-width, warm-started base-LM and multimodal dictionaries and says splitting and merging are near absent in that comparison. The control, steering, and task-ablation results concern other questions.
record.test_reason: The study's results do not bear on any version. It never varies SAE dictionary size, never tests parent/child absorption or hierarchy, and never compares training objectives on splitting. It mentions splitting only in App. E.2, where it matches a base-LM dictionary to a same-width, warm-started multimodal dictionary and notes that splitting/merging would show as relocation or emergence, which are near absent. That is a check on index correspondence across training stages, not a test of splitting with dictionary growth.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that MMDiff isolates multimodally adapted SAE features whose ablation selectively degrades spatial/OCR behaviour and unsafe responses, and whose steering improves spatial/OCR accuracy. They also conclude that mid-layer spatial features in PaliGemma 2 are largely acquired in multimodal fine-tuning. The correspondence result (preserved/rotated, no relocation) is a validation check in App. E.2, not a headline conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: No size-growth or split-measurement recipe is compared with the original claim's method.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE training regime affects decoder alignment: the paper reports that text-only SAEs remain aligned with the base dictionary, while image-only and full-sequence SAEs diverge in early layers before realigning deeper.

fits_no_version.finding: Full PaliGemma 2 dictionary matching: 96.41% of features preserved, 3.36% rotated in place, 0.00% relocated, 0.23% emergent. A cross-seed relocation rate of 0.44% is also reported (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warm-started, same-width SAE dictionaries adapted to a fine-tuned or multimodal model keep index correspondence, with few relocated or emergent features.

record.problems: The reported feature-matching result compares same-width, warm-started dictionaries across model stages rather than dictionaries of increasing size, so it does not resolve the size-dependent splitting claim.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; no additional results meeting the claim-specific row criteria were reported.

untested.parts: All: no change in dictionary size.
All: no size-related splitting analysis in large models or open SAE releases, although open Scope SAEs are used.
All: no feature-family or hierarchy analysis.
All: no absorption or parent/child firing test.
All: no comparison of larger and smaller SAEs.

All: no comparison of training objectives on splitting. The training regimes compared (text, image, full-sequence, random init) differ in loss mask and initialization, not in the sparsity objective, and alignment rather than splitting is measured.

record.verdict_notes: Splitting is mentioned only in passing in App. E.2. No verdicts are given because the study tests no version.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over dictionary size or test of coarse-to-fine feature splits.
The paper studies multiple MLLM families, but does not test size-related splitting across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families, conceptual hierarchies, or split-feature geometry.
No parent-child firing or absorption test, nor a test of whether SAE size or sparsity fixes absorption.
No comparison of larger and smaller SAEs for decompositions or novel latents; the reported dictionary matching is across same-width base and adapted dictionaries.
No test attributing splitting to the sparsity objective or comparing Matryoshka or other objectives on splitting.

rows.subject: PaliGemma 2
rows.operation_detail: Matched each feature in the full multimodal dictionary to its same-index and best-matching base-dictionary feature using decoder cosine.

conditions.value: base-LM SAE dictionary versus multimodal-adapted SAE dictionary

rows.value: Preserved: 96.41% (410,709); rotated in place: 3.36% (14,295); relocated: 0.00% (0); emergent: 0.23% (971).
rows.note: The paper says splitting and merging would appear as relocation or emergence and are near absent in this same-width, aligned-dictionary comparison. This does not test the claim's dictionary-size condition.
rows.check: Linking (none) and state are right. The subject is the Gemma-Scope JumpReLU SAE (16,384 features × 26 layers), adapted on PaliGemma 2 activations; the record lists the model only. This is a validation of the paper's own index-alignment method, so it serves as a method check rather than a claim result.

relation.reason: App. E.2 says splitting and merging would show as relocation or emergence, both near absent. That is a passing discussion in a validation check, not a test or a use of the finding.

tranche.reason: Compares same-width (16K) warm-started base-LM and multimodal-adapted dictionaries. Dictionary size, absorption/hierarchy and training objectives are never varied. Splitting is mentioned only to justify index alignment (App. E.2).

source_check.notes: Table 15 counts sum to 425,975, 9 short of 26x16,384 = 425,984; the percentages are unaffected. The near-absence of splitting/merging is about warm-started same-width fine-tuning on a new input distribution, not dictionary growth, so it bears on no version.

statements.correction: Table 15, full PaliGemma 2 dictionary: preserved 96.41% (410,709), rotated in place 3.36% (14,295), relocated 0.00% (0), emergent 0.23% (971). Cross-seed relocation 0.44% (about 72 of 16,384 per layer): different-seed SAEs on 8 layers, App. C.5, Table 9.
statements.problem: All numbers are in the text. 96.41/3.36/0.00/0.23 are from Table 15 (full 26x16,384 dictionary). 0.44% is the cross-seed relocation rate from App. C.5 (Table 9), a different-seed retrain on only the 8 layers with top spatial features. The statement keeps it as a separate sentence, as the text's E.2 paragraph does, so it is acceptable.
